description: A dedicated trio of innovators engineering the future of space medicine. Combining skills in embedded systems, UI/UX design, and data analytics, our 3-person team is building a real-time Astronaut Health Monitoring System to track crew vitals, predict health anomalies, and ensure peak astronaut performance in extreme space environments.
summary:
COSMOLOOKUP is an astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to help monitor physiological changes and identify potential health risks during space missions. It combines astronaut health indicators, historical trends, personalized exercise guidance, alerts, and an interactive 3D anatomical model to make complex health information easier to understand.

AI-assisted development tools were used for software architecture, coding, debugging, and integration. The platform incorporates NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) as a scientific research source, using publicly available spaceflight research datasets and metadata to inform health-risk analysis and provide scientific context. These research findings complement simulated astronaut monitoring data; they are not presented as live astronaut telemetry.

By bringing health indicators, research evidence, and explainable assessments together, COSMOLOOKUP aims to support timely, informed health-monitoring decisions and contribute to safer, longer-duration human space exploration.
details:
COSMOLOOKUP is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to address the challenges of maintaining astronaut health during long-duration space missions. It brings physiological monitoring, historical health trends, scientific research evidence, and interactive anatomical visualization into a unified mission-control interface.

The platform organizes astronaut health information into an interactive dashboard featuring a rotatable 3D human anatomical model. Users can explore different body systems, inspect relevant health indicators, identify potential concerns, view alerts, and access personalized exercise guidance. Its assessment system uses historical baselines, trend analysis, data freshness, and contextual health indicators to support explainable decision-making rather than autonomous diagnosis.

NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) is integrated as a source of publicly available spaceflight biological research datasets and metadata. These resources provide scientific context for understanding physiological changes associated with spaceflight. They complement clearly identified simulated astronaut monitoring data rather than being misrepresented as live telemetry.

AI tools assisted our development process through architecture exploration, code generation, debugging, testing, and integration. The technology stack includes React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, and NASA's research APIs. We also use Git and GitHub for version control and collaborative development.

The project's creativity lies in combining interactive 3D anatomy with explainable health assessments and research-backed context, making complex physiological information more accessible. Our team considered scientific accuracy, data reliability, usability, privacy, performance, and the limitations of spaceflight monitoring systems throughout development.

Our intended impact is to support better-informed health-monitoring decisions, encourage early attention to potential health risks, and contribute to safer and more sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.
